text_version.note: AGORA record covers part of an act: Section 106.11 Application: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Sex in Education Programs or Activities Receiving Federal

territorial_scope.description: Applies to a recipient's education program or activity in the United States; contributing conduct outside the program or outside the United States is taken into account, but the duty stays with the US recipient.

evidence.quote: a recipient has an obligation to address a sex-based hostile environment under its education program or activity in the United States, even when some conduct alleged to be contributing to the hostile environment occurred outside the recipient's education program or activity or outside the United States.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Final Title IX rule § 106.11 requires recipients of federal financial assistance to address sex-based harassment occurring under their education program or activity, including off-campus conduct they control or discipline. The excerpt is the preamble discussion, not the full regulatory text.
summary.long: Section 106.11 of the Title IX final regulations, as discussed in this excerpt, requires a recipient to address sex-based harassment under its education program or activity. The provision covers conduct in off-campus settings operated or overseen by the recipient, conduct subject to the recipient's disciplinary authority, conduct on school-sponsored devices, networks and digital platforms (including AI technologies), and training programs sponsored at other locations. The Department states that a recipient is responsible for conduct over which it has disciplinary authority or substantial control, and that the list of covered conduct is not exhaustive. The changed text extends the duty to a sex-based hostile environment in the United States even where contributing conduct occurred outside the program or outside the United States. The Department states that Title IX does not apply to sex-based harassment outside a recipient's education program or activity. The excerpt also records commenters' support and opposition and the Department's responses; these are context, not operative text.

relations.note: The text states that the Title IX statute authorizes the Department to regulate sex discrimination under any education program or activity of a recipient, and that the Department's regulatory authority is coextensive with that statute.

notes: The document is the preamble Discussion of § 106.11 in the final rule (section E, Application). The regulatory text of § 106.11 is not included, so no events, thresholds, obligations or enforcement are coded here. The agency and the rule are referred to only as 'the Department' and 'the final regulations' in the text. Some citations are printed without spaces (e.g., 'see20 U.S.C. 1687', 'See87 FR 41401'); quotes reproduce them as printed. The same Davis quotation is cited as 526 U.S. at 645 by a commenter and as 526 U.S. at 630 by the Department. The Discussion says the Department 'declines to provide additional examples' of covered conduct, yet it lists AI technologies among conduct that may fall under a recipient's program or activity, and states that the list is not exhaustive. The Department states that Title IX does not apply to harassment outside a recipient's program or activity, and also that the final rule covers hostile environments in the United States even when some contributing conduct occurred outside the program or activity or outside the United States; both formulations appear side by side. Court decisions (Davis, Gebser, Brown v. Arizona, Roe v. Marshall Univ.) and the unenacted H.R. 5396 are cited but are not coded as relations, since they are not registry instruments and no substantive interaction with this rule is stated. Spot-check: ai_sectoral added as a secondary domain because the Discussion places conduct via digital platforms 'including AI technologies' within a recipient's education program; extraterritorial removed from territorial scope because only contributing conduct, not actors, outside the United States is reached.
